title: The two scan questions P-L4-008 leaves open on f35v: two separate lobed leaves do sit below the crown, and the root is not clipped by a crop but drawn down to the page edge, long and hooked on the left, short and curled on the right
statement: P-L4-008 asks, besides a masked rating round that needs comparison plates I cannot reach from this seat, for two things to be settled on the Voynich drawing itself: whether two oak-like leaves genuinely sit below the crown, and how the roots end. I looked at f35v on the Yale scan (canvas 1006143, full size 2853 by 3769; regions pct:50,5,48,60 for the upper plant and pct:20,68,78,30 for the root, at 1500 and 1700 pixels). I had not seen the step's rubric or its comparison plates; I had seen the page before, for a second look at anchor N-005, and knew that it has been compared with ivy and with oak. Leaves below the crown: yes, two, unmistakably separate from the crown. One stands at the left about halfway down the stem, one at the right a little higher; each is a single flat blade on its own curved stalk, with five to seven rounded lobes a side divided by open rounded sinuses, painted the same dark green as the crown. Their stalks leave the thin pale side stems, not the main stem. The crown itself is drawn with the same lobed outline repeated many times and overlapping, so the two lower leaves read as the crown's leaf shown once in isolation. Other things in the same view that a rubric should have a line for: a sheaf of fine parallel lines running from the main stem up into the base of the crown; about fifteen clusters of round blue-green bodies, three to eight to a cluster, each cluster hanging from a thin looped stalk off the side stems, with two clusters partly painted red-brown low on the left; and two pale side stems that leave the base, bow outward and cross: I see one crossing low on the plant, where the two side stems pass over each other and the main stem, and a second higher up, where the left side stem arches over the main stem to the right. I count that as two crossings; the upper one is a side stem over the main stem, not the two side stems over each other, which a rubric line about a 'doubled crossing' should make explicit. Roots: the root is complete on the scan; nothing is cut off by the image. It is red-brown, with one long arm running left along the foot of the page and ending in three or four thin upturned hooks, a row of short downward fingers along its underside, and on the right two or three short thick arms that curl back on themselves. The lowest fingers end at or within a hair of the lower edge of the leaf, so whether a few tips were lost when the leaf was trimmed cannot be told from the scan; the outline shows no finger that is plainly severed. So on the two criteria the step says no comparator met: a double crossing of stems is there in the sense just described, and the root is strongly lopsided and hooked as described. I add no score for any comparator and no opinion on ivy or oak; on this page the fruit clusters and the twining stems point one way and the leaf shape another, which is the step's own conclusion.
check: On the two regions named, a second observer answers yes or no to: two isolated lobed leaves below the crown; two crossings of the side stems; a root with one long left arm ending in upturned hooks and short curled arms on the right; any root finger visibly cut by the page edge. Then run the step's masked rating round with observers who can reach the comparison plates.
